Randomly Subsample a Batch of FASTA or Paired-End FASTQ Files

Source: R/vtamR_fun.R
random_sample_batch.Rd

Randomly subsamples sequences from multiple FASTA files or paired-end FASTQ files described in an input information file. The sampling size can be specified as a fixed number of reads per file (n), a proportion of reads per file (p), or a total number of reads across all files (N).

Usage

random_sample_batch(
  info,
  dir,
  outdir,
  n = NULL,
  p = NULL,
  N = NULL,
  chunk_lines = 1e+05,
  randseed = NULL,
  compress = FALSE,
  compress_method = "R",
  pigz_path = NULL,
  num_threads = 0,
  fast_count = TRUE,
  sep = ",",
  quiet = TRUE,
  log_file = NULL
)

Arguments

info

Character string with path to the input information file or data frame describing the sequence files. The file must contain either a fasta column or both fastq_fw and fastq_rv columns. An optional read_count column may contain the number of reads in each file.

dir

Character string. Directory containing the input sequence files listed in info.

outdir

Character string. Directory where the subsampled sequence files and updated information file will be written.

n

Numeric or integer. Number of reads to randomly sample from each input file. If a file contains fewer than n reads, all reads are retained. Mutually exclusive with p and N.

p

Numeric. Proportion of reads to randomly sample from each input file. Must typically be between 0 and 1. The number of sampled reads is calculated by rounding p * read_count. Mutually exclusive with n and N.

N

Integer. Total number of reads to sample across all input files. Reads are allocated proportionally according to the number of reads in each file. If N is greater than or equal to the total number of reads, no proportional reduction is applied. Mutually exclusive with n and p.

chunk_lines

Numeric. Number of lines to process at a time when counting or sampling sequences. Larger values may improve performance but require more memory. Defaults to 1e5.

randseed

Numeric or integer, or NULL. Random seed used to make sampling reproducible. If NULL, no seed is explicitly set.

compress

Logical. If TRUE, output sequence files are compressed and output filenames are generated accordingly. Defaults to FALSE.

compress_method

Character string. Must be one of "pigz", "gzip", or "R". Compression method used when writing output files. Defaults to "R". Only relevant when a file has fewer sequences than required and is copied to the output directory with a different compression state than the input.

pigz_path

Optional path to the pigz executable. If NULL (default), resolved via getOption("vtamR.pigz_path") or the PATH (see get_path).

num_threads

Positive integer: number of CPU threads to use. If 0, all available CPUs are used. Only relevant when a file has fewer sequences than required and is copied to the output directory with a different compression state than the input.

fast_count

Logical. If TRUE, uses the faster read-counting method implemented by count_reads(). Defaults to TRUE. Available only in linux-like sytems.

sep

Character string. Field separator used to read and write the information file. Defaults to ",".

quiet

Logical. If TRUE, suppresses progress and informational messages where supported. Defaults to TRUE.

log_file

Character string specifying the path to the CSV log file. The path is resolved with the following priority:

  1. the log_file argument, if explicitly provided by the user;

  2. the vtamR.log_file option set with options(vtamR.log_file = ...), if set;

  3. "vtamR_log.csv" in the current working directory, used as a last resort if neither of the above is set.

To disable logging entirely, set log_file = NA.

Value

A data frame containing the updated information table. Input sequence file columns are replaced with the names of the subsampled output files, and a read_count column is added containing the number of reads retained after sampling. The updated information table is also written to outdir using the basename of info.

Details

Exactly one of n, p, or N must be specified. When read counts are not available in the input information file, they are calculated automatically. The function then performs random subsampling on each input file and writes the resulting files and an updated information file to outdir.

For FASTA input, the information file must contain a fasta column. For paired-end FASTQ input, it must contain both fastq_fw and fastq_rv columns. An optional read_count column can be supplied to avoid recounting reads in the input files.

The function first determines whether the input describes FASTA files or paired-end FASTQ files. If read counts are missing or incomplete, all input files are counted using count_reads().

Sampling is then performed independently for each file:

  • With n, up to n reads are sampled from each file.

  • With p, the same proportion of reads is sampled from each file.

  • With N, reads are allocated proportionally across all files based on their original read counts.

FASTA files are processed with random_sample_fasta(), while paired-end FASTQ files are processed with random_sample_fastq(). For paired-end FASTQ data, forward and reverse reads are sampled together to preserve pairing.

The function determines whether the input describes FASTA files or paired-end FASTQ files and writes the combined updated information table to fastainfo.csv or fastqinfo.csv, respectively.

See also

random_sample_fasta(), random_sample_fastq(), count_reads(), fast_copy(), smart_gzip().

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Sample up to 1000 reads from each file
random_sample_batch(
  info = "samples.csv",
  dir = "input_sequences",
  outdir = "subsampled_sequences",
  n = 1000
)

# Sample 10% of reads from each file
random_sample_batch(
  info = "samples.csv",
  dir = "input_sequences",
  outdir = "subsampled_sequences",
  p = 0.1,
  randseed = 123
)

# Sample approximately 1 million reads distributed proportionally
# across all input files
random_sample_batch(
  info = "samples.csv",
  dir = "input_sequences",
  outdir = "subsampled_sequences",
  N = 1e6
)
} # }
